findings.summary: Invocation ownership leaks into unchanged unqualified and parameter flat calls
findings.evidence: Native compiled control at HEAD 975c73b49def2813517b00c296006417d062d8b2: existing check-flat fixture extended with direct_run () = root_body 3, unknown_run root_body = root_body 3, bare_callback xs = List.map root_body xs. Old fb9c8f3 extractor and current extractor linked against the same current collector. All three b.ml rows change callee_file from a.ml to NULL although none uses a qualified alias. Native pending probe separately confirms unchanged heads (direct Head_local, unknown callback_param, bare callback Head_enumerated) with ownership context off/on. Equality assertion exits 1 after successful native setup; build exits 0. Alias-owned target-name membership applies to every ordinary row, so introducing Bridge.alias = root_body changes unrelated existing facts.
findings.fix: Carry occurrence-level owned-target provenance from the collector to the flat consumer and apply the new alias attribution only to supported qualified invocation occurrences. Preserve legacy direct, parameter and bare-callback rows and existing point-free behavior; add the native three-form regression controls. A Head_enumerated-only guard is insufficient because bare local callbacks have that head too.
